research_rationale: Executive Order 13348 of July 22, 2004 (69 FR 44885) blocked property of Charles Taylor, his associates and persons determined by the Treasury, prohibited imports of Liberian round logs and timber products, and declared a national emergency under IEEPA and the NEA. It was a standing emergency order. Executive Order 13710 of November 12, 2015 (80 FR 71679, held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13710.txt) states: "Accordingly, I hereby terminate the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13348, revoke that order, and further order:" and "This order is effective at 2:00 p.m. eastern standard time on November 12, 2015." The status history for this order holds one editorial API observation (continuation notices of 2005-2010 and the revocation entry) and no event ending the order earlier. Every clause therefore ended on November 12, 2015 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. Status route: undecided, so this sheet awaits status review.
savings_reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 13710, citing section 202(a) of the NEA, says termination "shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to the effective date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to the effective date of this order." This preserves accrued matters only; it continues no operative clause, and the blocking and import-ban commands themselves ended.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order number with cruden.py number EO:13348 (30 matches in 14 files, untruncated). Hits are the original, Executive Order 13710 (APP mirror and FR text) and the Treasury continuation notices of 2005-2015 (e.g. fr-2015-18044, July 17, 2015). The continuation notices continue the emergency; none ends or amends a clause. The three bounded machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr, 0 hits; later-events:ofr_catalog, 9 hits being the notices and the revocation) were read for coverage. No earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or own-terms end was found. Section 10 gives only an effective time, not an end.
scope_check: Executive Order 13710 revokes "that order", the whole of Executive Order 13348, so no partial revocation question arises; it contains no exception for any section. The Annex persons and Treasury designations were exercised under section 1 and ended with it.
independent_command_check: Each clause was read against the held original text. Sections 1 and 2 issue blocking and import commands under IEEPA and UNPA which depend on the declared emergency; Executive Order 13710 terminated that emergency and revoked the order together. Sections 3-8 depend on sections 1-2, and sections 9-11 are non-operative or one-time provisions covered clause by clause. No clause rests on a separate statute or independent authority that would survive revocation.
savings_check: See savings reason: Executive Order 13710 section 1 preserves accrued actions, rights and penalties only.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13362 of November 29, 2004 (69 FR 70173) was a standing Vacancies Act succession order adding five FEMA regional directors to the line of succession to the Secretary of Homeland Security behind the officers named in section 88 of Executive Order 13286. Section 2 of Executive Order 13442 of August 13, 2007 (72 FR 45877, 45878) revokes it by name: "Executive Order 13362 of November 29, 2004 ( ‘‘Designation of Additional Officers for the Department of Homeland Security Order of Succession’’), is hereby revoked." The held text of 6 U.S.C. 111 notes the same revocation. Every clause ended on August 13, 2007, so the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. Status route: undecided, so this sheet awaits status review.
savings_reason: The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 13442 contains only the amendment of section 88 of Executive Order 13286 (section 1) and the revocation (section 2); it has no savings, transition or continuation wording, and a search of the held corpus for the order number found no other instrument that preserves any effect of Executive Order 13362.
earlier_end_check: cruden.py number EO:13362 found four matching files: the original (FR and APP copies), Executive Order 13442 and the 6 U.S.C. 111 note that records its revocation. No earlier revocation, supersession or expiry was found. Section 1 runs "until such time as" an officer able to act exists, a contingent condition within each vacancy; no held source shows a vacancy that triggered it or that it ended. The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage; the OFR catalog records the revocation by Executive Order 13442.
scope_check: Section 2 of Executive Order 13442 revokes the whole order by name and title, not a part; section 1 of Executive Order 13442 separately amends section 88 of Executive Order 13286 and is an amendment of another order, not an end of this one.
independent_command_check: All clauses are parts of one succession designation; the recital, the section 1 designation and the section 2 exceptions all depend on the designation. The authority cited is the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998, which is not repealed by the revocation but is a general statute that supplies no independent command surviving the order.
savings_check: No savings wording in Executive Order 13442 and no other held instrument preserving effects of this order; see savings reason.
